prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 (policy-focused, non-ideological; ≤500 words)

- Tax, pay and pensions
  - Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rise in income tax or VAT rates.
  - “Triple Lock Plus”: state pension and a new age‑related personal allowance to rise by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; maintain existing pensioner benefits.
  - Clamp down on tax non‑compliance to raise £6bn a year.

- Family support and childcare
  - 30 hours free childcare from nine months to school start by Sept 2025; wraparound care by Sept 2026.
  - Move Child Benefit to a household test: taper between £120k–£160k household income.

- Welfare and work
  - Reform disability benefits (PIP) and work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes to specialist assessors.
  - Accelerate Universal Credit rollout; tougher sanctions for long‑term non‑compliance; new Fraud Bill.

- Education and skills
  - Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid military placements or civic service).
  - 100,000 additional apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑outcome degree courses.
  - Advanced British Standard for 16–19; statutory school-day mobile phone ban; expand SEN places; parental access to teaching materials.

- Health and social care
  - NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgery builds/modernisations; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres; 40 new hospitals by 2030.
  - £3.4bn tech plan: NHS App as single front door; AI and imaging upgrades; reduce managers by 5,500.
  - Dental recovery plan (2.5m extra appointments, rural “golden hellos”, NHS service requirement for new dentists).
  - Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health expansion; implement Cass Review; mental health school teams to 100% coverage by 2030 and community hubs nationwide.
  - Full compensation for infected blood victims.

- Policing and justice
  - 8,000 additional neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law; lawful facial recognition.
  - Tougher sentences for serious and domestic offences; new offences (spiking, deepfakes); four new prisons; cut court backlogs.

- Immigration and borders
  - Legal annual cap on work/family visas, falling yearly and set by Parliament.
  - Maintain higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks/IHS; implement Illegal Migration Act; removals to Rwanda; more returns deals; Parliament‑set cap on safe/legal routes.

- Economy, business and regulation
  - Meet fiscal rules (debt falling; borrowing <3% GDP in year 5).
  - Maintain corporation tax rate; full expensing (seek to extend to leasing); SME 10‑point plan (business rates relief, prompt payments, Open Finance, Invest in Women Fund).
  - Public R&D to £22bn; compute clusters; Advanced Manufacturing Plan; maintain R&D tax reliefs.
  - Trade: implement CPTPP; pursue FTAs (India, GCC); uphold TCA without CJEU alignment.
  - Regulatory reform using post‑Brexit freedoms; reduce civil service to pre‑pandemic size; cut consultants; expand AI skills in government.

- Energy and climate
  - Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; new gas power stations.
  - Treble offshore wind; launch CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; progress Wylfa; more interconnectors.
  - £6bn for home energy efficiency plus universal voucher scheme; retain price cap; Pumpwatch; local electricity markets.
  - No new green levies; fracking moratorium; protect top-grade farmland from solar; onshore wind with local consent; import carbon pricing by 2027.

- Housing and planning
  - Build 1.6m homes; scrap nutrient neutrality via developer mitigation; fast‑track brownfield in 20 largest cities; urban development corporations; protect Green Belt.
  - Permanent Stamp Duty relief for first‑time buyers to £425k; new Help to Buy; extend Mortgage Guarantee.
  - Leasehold reform (cap ground rents, curb forfeiture); Renters Reform (end Section 21 after court changes); CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; clamp down on problem holiday lets and illegal encampments.

- Transport and infrastructure
  - Reallocate £36bn HS2 savings to regional schemes; £8.3bn for roads/potholes; Northern Powerhouse Rail/Midlands Rail Hub elements; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing by local/metro authorities; referendums for new 20mph/LTN schemes; reverse London ULEZ expansion.
  - Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; nationwide contactless pay‑as‑you‑go.

- Communities, rural, environment and farming
  - £20m endowments for 105 towns (+30 more); extend Community Ownership Fund and UK Shared Prosperity Fund; expand Freeports/Investment Zones.
  - Farming budget +£1bn over Parliament (inflation‑linked); legal food security target and index; farm infrastructure fast‑track; renew £100m UK Seafood Fund.
  - Flood defence funding maintained; Plan for Water (tougher penalties, river recovery network, regulatory reform); tree/peat programmes; 11th National Park; anti–fly‑tipping measures; limit new incinerators; deep‑sea mining moratorium; Global Oceans Treaty ratification.

- Equality, online safety and governance
  - Clarify in law that Equality Act “sex” means biological sex; single legal sex; school duties on gender‑questioning guidance and parental notification.
  - Enforce Online Safety Act; consult on enhanced parental controls.
  - Maintain FPTP; voter ID; uphold devolved settlements; invest directly across UK nations; implement Windsor Framework and NI legacy arrangements.

- Culture, sport and media
  - Continue grassroots sports investment; Independent Football Regulator; women’s sport funding.
  - Creative tax incentives; flexible apprenticeships; night‑time economy review; BBC funding review focused on impartiality; access‑to‑cash via banking hubs; Post Office redress scheme delivery.
